summary: This article explains how the bicycle developed, how pedals, chains, and gears make it move, why cycling is healthy and efficient, and how riders race and stay safe.
introduce: Show the title “Cycling: Pedal Power” and give pairs one minute to list everything they already know about this topic. Share a few ideas on the board, then tell students to check which ideas the article confirms.

keyTerms.def: a part of a bike that makes pedaling easier or harder
doing a job well without wasting energy, time, or materials
a hard hat that keeps your head safe

challengeTerms.def: filled with or worked by air under pressure
shaped to move through air with little resistance
the ability to keep going for a long time

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that riding a bike is better than riding in a car for short trips? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how changes to the bicycle's design made riding safer and easier.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review gear, efficient, and helmet, and let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use pneumatic, aerodynamic, and endurance in a short paragraph that connects the article to something they learned in another subject.
